pr_title: Flexible trading days per year property
pr_body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

#### Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
Create new algorithm settings' property: `TradingDaysPerYear`. Which help user setup custom value for different brokerage or use in default state.
Characteristics of new property:
- [x] may be changeable by user
- [x] return diferent value depend on Brokerage
- [x] have defaul value

1. remove hardcoded values.
2. increase quality calculation in `PortfolioStatistics`

issue_context.title: AlgorithmPerformance instantiates PortfolioStatistics with the default tradingDaysPerYear = 252 regardless of securities
issue_context.body:
<!--- This template provides sections for bugs and features. Please delete any irrelevant sections before submitting -->

#### Expected Behavior
<!--- Required. Describe the behavior you expect to see for your case. -->
I would assume that tradingDaysPerYear accounts for the Brokerage model being used.

#### Actual Behavior
<!--- Required. Describe the actual behavior for your case. -->
It seems that AlgorithmPerformance doesn't do that and assumes the default tradingDaysPerYear = 252 regardless of securities. Unless I'm missing a compensating effect, this has serious consequences for instance for crypto as it would ruin annual performance and Sharpe ratio.

#### Potential Solution
<!--- Optional. Describe any potential solutions and/or thoughts as to what may be causing the difference between expected and actual behavior. -->
I haven't looked in detail, but I guess tapping into the securities market hours shouldn't be too hard.

#### Reproducing the Problem
<!--- Required for Bugs. Describe how to reproduce the problem. This can be via a failing unit test or a simplified algorithm that reliably demonstrates this issue.  -->

Well launching a crypto backtest and placing a breakpoint at https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/master/Common/Statistics/PortfolioStatistics.cs#L249 to figure out how Sharpe ratio was computed made me find out about it. 

#### System Information
<!--- Required for Bugs. Include any system specific information, such as OS. -->
Windows Server 2019

comments:
- Add a new `IAlgorithmSettings` property `int? TradingDaysPerYear`
- Add same property to `AlgorithmConfiguration` set by from `algorithm.Settings`, this is so that the report generator can access it too -> report generator should start using this value (if != 0 for backwards compatibility case, handling previous version results)
- After algorithm initialization, based on the brokerage model we can default to 252 or 365 as `TradingDaysPerYear` value, if it hasn't been set by the algorithm
- Adjust all hardcoded `252` values in the lean engine statistics calculation to start using the setting

review_comments: Could just assert the actual expected value with  `AreEqual`
This is not really necessary, we just need to assert the trading days per year value
